items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law and the tax law, in relation to the healthy options and community outreach program and to direct the empire state development corporation to establish a public awareness campaign regarding such program
items.lawCode: Add Art 29-A §520, Ag & Mkts L; amd §§210-B & 606, Tax L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S943

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law and the tax law, in
relation to the healthy options and community outreach program and to
direct the empire state development corporation to establish a public
awareness campaign regarding such program

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To establish the healthy options and community outreach program

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the agriculture and markets law adding article 29-A
creating the healthy options and community outreach program.

Section two amends the tax law by adding a new subdivision 49 of
section 210-B to create the credit for convenience stores and small
grocers who participate in the healthy options and community outreach
program.

Section three amends the tax law adding a new subsection (ccc) to
section 606 to include the credit for convenience stores and small
grocers who participate in the healthy options and community outreach
program.

Section four ensures that the empire state development corporation
develop, establish and implement a public awareness campaign regarding
the healthy options and community outreach program, to include
information on the benefits of healthy eating and the availability of
those foods and beverages in the local community.

Section five sets forth the effective date

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 2009, New York state created a program called Healthy Food and
Healthy Communities fund which provides financing to supermarket and
grocery operators to open stores in places across the state that may
not have access to fresh nutritious foods This bill would build upon
that program by encouraging small store operators to upgrade their
facilities if needed in order to offer healthier options. There are
many areas across the state without a grocery store nearby, making the
local bodega or convenience store the only place to stop for grocery
needs.  This bill provides tax credits for owners who commit to
selling healthy food and drinks at their shops of up to 100% of the
cost over five years if they have to expand, purchase coolers or
shelving for the purposes of selling these products. But, access to
healthy foods is only part of the solution; Empire State Development
Corporation will be tasked with implementing a public awareness
campaign to explain the benefits of healthy eating as well as where to
go to get them. This statewide program is based on a program adopted
in New York city in 2006 to expand the options and demand for healthy
foods at their corner stores and bodegas in areas with the highest
poverty and chronic disease. New York city found that store owners can
only stock what people will buy, so it was important to have a public
awareness campaign in order to sustain the healthy changes they were
looking for They also found that there needs to be a variety of
approaches, with a lot of support and assistance in connecting store
owners with the healthy food suppliers and farmers, training on how to
purchase, price and store fresh produce as well as how to present it
in store.  Advertising and promotional materials were key to the store
owners' success. This bill builds upon the successes of New York city
and takes it statewide with the help of Empire State Development
corporation, and the Department of Agriculture and Markets. Funds will
be spent in targeted communities across New York state with store
owners who are interested in participating and make the long term
commitment to ensure citizens have new and continuing access to
healthy options.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.5432A of 2015-2016; Passed Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided that sections two and
three of this act shall apply to taxable years beginning on and after
January 1, 2018.
